ledger.claim: The length of this trip is governed by the GPS trace, which measures 22.26 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff, not by the 22.3 km figure carried on the trip record: POL-RD-01 says in terms that trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The fare on EV-FARE-00528 was nevertheless billed on distance_charged_km 22.3, i.e. on the rounded copy the clause disfavours, so the charge rests on a figure the governing clause tells the tribunal not to use.

Nothing on this record excuses the distance the driver actually ran, and the rider closes those doors now. The traffic-advisory artifact for this trip is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-00528-01 has no payload, carries weight 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no advisory can be pointed to under POL-RD-03 to exonerate any excess. The chat log for TRP-00528 (EV-CHAT-00528, complete, weight 1.0) is empty — message_count 0 — so no rider-requested detour or additional stop can be made out under POL-RD-04 either. The driver's 'normal trip, normal route' is the only thing on file in his favour.

The rider does not press a distance-deviation claim, because the arithmetic does not support one and the rider will not put a number in front of the tribunal that the record contradicts. Measured on the governing trace the excess over the 22.1 km optimal is 0.16 km, or 0.72% of optimal — below both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates, which require an excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal. No deviation is established on this trip.

What is left is small, but it is arithmetic the platform has already run on its own ledger, and it is the rider's money. EV-FARE-00528 charges distance on 22.3 km and time on 38.0 min against an optimal of 22.1 km and 36.0 min, and the fare breakdown's own recomputation under POL-RD-02 prices the trip at 43.4370 against a charged_total of 44.44 — a difference of 1.0030, which rounds up to 1.05. The rider asks the tribunal to settle that line on the fare rather than leave it standing unexamined; it is the only distance-and-time correction this record will support, and it should be stated on the face of the ruling.

The rider also does not maintain the arithmetic pleaded in the filed claim. The trip record shows the estimate displayed at booking was 58-62 before surge, and the ledger's charged_total is 44.44 — below that figure, not above it — and the fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 gives the rider no quote-versus-charge difference to claim. The rider's complaint is about how this trip was billed, not about a fare that exceeded the price shown.

On the present state of the record the tribunal cannot say what NO_ACTION would preserve. EV-FARE-00528 records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, while the rider's account is that the difference was already refunded and a voucher issued. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 leaves exactly that conflict as it stands — the charge stays collected — whereas ESCALATE holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it. The rider asks that the amount be held for a human reviewer rather than left as a charge whose state the record does not agree on.

The route-deviation threshold in POL-RD-01 is not met on the governing measurement. The GPS trace runs 22.26 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 22.1 km: an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.724% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 makes a deviation ESTABLISHED only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both gates must pass. Both fail here by more than an order of magnitude. The excess is not merely below the materiality gate, it is below the ordinary establishment gate, so no deviation exists on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the drive.

There is no reading of the distance fields on which the rider succeeds. POL-RD-01 states expressly that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs and that trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy which may NOT be cited for the threshold test. On the trace figure the excess is 0.16 km; on the rounded 22.3 km copy it is 0.2 km. The two figures do not straddle the 0.8 km absolute gate the way POL-RD-01's drafting note contemplates, because neither of them approaches it. Whichever field the rider reaches for, the establishment test fails.

The trace that carries the measurement is clean, so there is no gap in the record for the rider to exploit. EV-GPS-00528 records 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, from first fix 08:16:40 to last fix 08:54:40. None of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs fires: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The excess is therefore measured from an unimpaired trace, no independent corroboration is required, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger cannot fire.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and does not discharge it. Limb (a) is satisfied in form — the trip identifier TRP-00528 runs consistently through the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the pickup timestamp is common to them — but limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace, and the derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. The burden never shifts to the driver, no exculpatory clause under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 needs to be run, and the rider's claim fails at the threshold it was required to cross.

The residue route left open by POL-RD-01 — a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists — affords the rider nothing here. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all and an ERP total of 0.00, and no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport). Every charged line corresponds to this trip's own recorded movement: base fare 3.80, metered distance on 22.3 km, metered time on 38.0 minutes, the 1.4 surge recorded on the fare breakdown, and the 0.80 platform fee. There is no unmatched charge line for POL-RD-09(4) to correct.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03, and on this rider-filed dispute it preserves the present payment state. The ledger records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so no refund has in fact issued and the driver's metered fare stands intact. The rider's assertion that a support manager 'refunded the difference plus a voucher' is supported by no artifact in the bundle; on the only payment artifact before the tribunal, the charge is live and nothing has been returned.

The rider's own narrative does not survive contact with the artifacts. The claim text asserts the trip carried 'no surge', but POL-RD-02 fixes the surge multiplier on fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else, and that field reads 1.4. The claim text asserts a fare of 'ninety-one sixty' against an estimate of sixty, but the only fare artifact records total_charged 44.44, quoted_fare_sgd null and a distance-and-time charge built at the metered rate card — a figure lower than the estimate range carried on the trip record, not higher. No artifact in the bundle supports the figures on which the rider's complaint is constructed.

No repeat-deviation uplift is available and none is needed. POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, or where the evidence is otherwise finely balanced; on this trace there is no deviation at all, material or otherwise. For completeness, the driver's trailing-90-day deviation flag count is 0 against 250 completed trips in the same window, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test could be satisfied even if the clause were engaged. Limb (b)'s uplift and limb (c)'s conduct referral are simply not in play.

None of POL-RD-10's mandatory escalation triggers fires on this record. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; the timestamps do not disagree — the trace opens at 08:16:40 on the trip record's started_at and closes at 08:54:40 on its ended_at; and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record. There is no basis for holding the disputed amount rather than ruling on it.

The bundle's one missing artifact is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00528-01, which carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; I disclose that impairment expressly. Its absence cannot make this record incomplete, because an advisory's only function in this policy is to justify or reduce an excess that POL-RD-01 has already established, and there is no excess on this trace to reduce. No party needs the document for any fact the ruling turns on, so the absence is citable but immaterial.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this dispute is about whether the trip was overcharged through a route deviation. On the evidence it was not, and no money moves.

Distance. Both sides and the record agree on the measurement. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace figure governing: trace_distance_km is 22.26 km against a booked optimal of 22.1 km, an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.72% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only if the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms AND 20% of optimal; both gates must pass, and both fail here by more than an order of magnitude. No deviation is established, and the clause says expressly that where a gate fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. I accept the driver's threshold claims and the rider's own concession of the same arithmetic. The rider's related point — that the charge was metered on the rounded 22.3 km copy rather than the governing 22.26 km trace — does not help: POL-RD-01's non-citation rule governs the threshold test, not the meter, and the 0.04 km difference produces no excess and no refund right.

The fare and the rider's figures. The filed claim speaks of a charge of 91.60 and of 'no surge'. The only fare artifact (EV-FARE-00528, weight 1.0) records total_charged 44.44, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and it carries surge_multiplier 1.4 — POL-RD-02 fixes the surge on fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else. The booking estimate shown was 58-62 before surge, so the charge sits below the estimate, not above it, and the trip was METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 gives no quote-versus-charge difference. The 91.60 figure and the 'no surge' assertion appear in no artifact and cannot carry a finding. The rider's account that a manager already refunded the difference and issued a voucher is equally unsupported: the ledger shows no refund.

The 1.05 the rider asks for. The fare breakdown carries a recomputation pricing the trip at 43.4370 against 44.44 — a difference of 1.0030, rounding to 1.05. That arithmetic is POL-RD-02, and POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. No deviation is established, so the clause never engages and the 1.05 is not a live entitlement; it is what the arithmetic would yield if the gates had been crossed. I decline it, and NO_ACTION leaves the 44.44 charge standing.

Billing integrity. The one route open regardless of deviation — POL-RD-09(4) — gives nothing: there are no ERP gantry lines (ERP total 0.00), no airport surcharge, and every charge line (base fare 3.80, metered distance and time, the 1.4 surge, the 0.80 platform fee) matches this trip's own recorded movement. There is no phantom line to refund.

Exculpation and escalation. The threshold failure decides the case before any exculpatory clause is needed, but I record that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00528-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, code MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed by the driver) and the chat log EV-CHAT-00528 is empty, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-04 could not have been run in any event. The GPS trace is clean — 229 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds — so POL-RD-07 does not impair it and no POL-RD-10(3) trigger exists. Reviewing the other escalation triggers: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the timestamps agree (the trace opens 08:16:40 and closes 08:54:40 on the trip's started_at and ended_at); no charge line is unmatched; and the rider's unsubstantiated narrative does not put the two sides on comparable admissible evidence. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so I rule rather than escalate, and no clause produces a referral.

On the rider's request to hold the amount because the record 'does not agree' on the payment state: POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative, and on this rider-filed dispute it leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand. An unrecorded earlier conversation is not evidence of a refund and does not change the ruling on this trip. If the platform wishes to look into that earlier support exchange, that question belongs to a human reviewer; it is not a clause-mandated referral and it does not hold the disputed amount.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The charge of 44.44 stands, no refund is due to the rider and no compensation to the driver, and no referral arises. Confidence 0.90, resting on the GPS trace and trip record, both at weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
